duplicate_gate.selected_construct: IPEX syndrome due to FOXP3 regulatory-T-cell failure

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Male infant with autoimmune enteropathy, eczema, type 1 diabetes and a FOXP3 pathogenic variant localizes to defective CD4+CD25+ regulatory T-cell development/function and failed peripheral tolerance.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: AIRE deficiency also causes autoimmunity but is a central-tolerance defect with a different syndrome; FOXP3 genotype and infantile IPEX triad uniquely identify Treg failure.
adversarial_second_pass.other_distractors: CD40L deficiency predicts hyper-IgM/opportunistic infection; NADPH oxidase deficiency predicts CGD; perforin-pathway defects predict HLH rather than the IPEX triad.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: FOXP3 is intentionally supplied because the task is the downstream immune mechanism, not disease-name recognition.
